# The subgroup generated by rank-one centralizer intersections

Author: Worker 1746.

This internal supporting unit names the two subgroups in the existing
`RootGeneratedCentralizerRankOneStatement` and proves the normality needed
for its normalizer-quotient argument. It does not prove that statement.
All points and root groups are the existing actual scheme-defined ones.

For an arbitrary field `k : Type u`, an affine group scheme `G`, and a map
`i : S.toGrp ⟶ G` from a commutative group scheme, the subgroup interfaces are:

- `relativeRootGeneratedSubgroup i`: the subgroup generated by the rational
  points of the actual root groups for all `a ∈ relativeRoots i`, reused
  from `Rational.RootGeneratedSubgroup`.
- `RelativeRoot.oppositeGeneratedPoints i a`: the subgroup generated by the
  actual groups for `a` and `-a`. The character `a` need not be a root.
- `RelativeRoot.rankOneCentralizerGeneratedPoints i`: the subgroup generated
  by `centralizerPoints i ⊓ oppositeGeneratedPoints i a` for all roots `a`.
  This is definitionally the right-hand side of the existing target.

The proof of `rankOneCentralizerGeneratedPoints_le_centralizer` applies
closure minimality to the first component of each intersection. If the
root set is closed under negation, the opposite groups lie in
`relativeRootGeneratedSubgroup i`, so `rankOneCentralizerGeneratedPoints_le_inf` proves
the reverse inclusion to the target. Negation stability is an explicit
premise of this reverse-inclusion lemma; it is not derived here. If the
root set is empty, both generated subgroups are trivial, and the required
inclusion follows without further premises.

If the underlying scheme morphism of `i` is a monomorphism, the normalizer
conjugation theorem already proved in `Rational.RootSubgroupConjugation`
transports the groups for `a` and `-a` to those for `w(a)` and `-w(a)`.
Closure minimality extends this transport to `oppositeGeneratedPoints`.
The normalizer also preserves the root set and the whole-torus centralizer.
It therefore takes each generator of `rankOneCentralizerGeneratedPoints`
to another such generator. The subgroup normalizer criterion for a closure
then proves
`normalizerPoints i ≤ Subgroup.normalizer (rankOneCentralizerGeneratedPoints i)`.
Since the generated subgroup lies in the whole-torus centralizer and hence
in the normalizer, this gives its normality as a subgroup of the rational
normalizer. No reductivity, maximal splitness, root-system realization,
Bruhat decomposition, Coxeter system or opposite factor-pair hypothesis
is used in this normality proof.

The provenance is an internal derivation by subgroup closure and the
published actual conjugation lemmas. It supplies the normality step for a
future quotient proof. Identifying the centralizer intersection of the
root-generated subgroup with this normal subgroup remains open.
